prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Helpful changes: Reordering onboarding flows, targeted functional hints (photo upload, path helper, identity security), select layouts (card carousel, single-click identity), key desktop flows (summon, visibility & control), and specific shortcut copy delivered significant wins.
Harmful changes: Major structural overhauls (split personality redesign, docking setup flow), spotlight path layouts, account persistence hints, and certain copy changes caused severe performance drops or early test cutoffs.
No effect seen: No effect was seen from wait, progress, and status indicators, background notifications, tutorial or prep screens, and incentive badges.
Predictions too high: High predictions (+8.0% or above) consistently overestimated actual impact, frequently yielding no effect seen or severe performance drops.
Predictions too low: Key winning changes—especially desktop control flows, shortcut copy, summon tests, and story-first reordering—far exceeded low or negative predictions.

Changes:
0: [finish, new_flow] Desktop Interactive Voice & Chat Switch Flow: Introduces an interactive desktop voice and text interaction setup module right on the home_intro screen to guide users through communicating with their companion. (why: Support mail shows confusion around how to control, hide, or talk to the pet after onboarding (3 emails).)
1: [adoption, new_screen] Custom Pet Creation Verification Screen: Inserts a dedicated pet design verification screen right after photo uploads to allow users to review and adjust parameters before rendering. (why: Adoption step drops to 64.2% and support receives complaints about custom pets failing or looking incorrect (3 emails).)
2: [sign_in, reorder] Late Account Sign-In Flow Reorder: Reorders sign_in to occur after adoption certificate customization, placing it right before the waiting screen to preserve pet creation data. (why: Users experience account resets and missing pets after signing in early or re-signing in (8 support emails).)
3: [choose_path, redesign] Compact Path Selector Layout Redesign: Replaces the existing path options layout on choose_path with a compact view that highlights core path differences clearly. (why: The choose_path step has a mean duration of 514s, suggesting users spend unnecessary time deciding between options.)
4: [sign_in, hint] Account Session Recovery Guidance Hint: Displays a supportive hint on the sign-in screen explaining how signing into an existing account restores previous pets. (why: Support received 8 emails about pets missing or reset after signing in again.)
5: [finish, copy] Desktop Hide and Show Keybind Copy: Updates the headline and body on home_intro to emphasize the instant hide/show hotkey command. (why: 3 support emails reported confusion on how to control or hide the desktop pet after setup.)
6: [adoption, layout] Split View Adoption Certificate Layout: Changes the layout of adoption_certificate screen to 'split' layout for better visual clarity while naming your companion. (why: Adoption step drop-off is highest at 64.2%, with a high median time of 89s.)
7: [home, hint] Background Generation Completion Hint: Adds a clear hint to the waiting screen explaining that pet creation continues safely in the background even if minimized. (why: Home/waiting median time is 201s with long tail mean of 2336s, showing users need reassurance during pet generation.)

scores.note: Desktop interaction setup addresses support feedback but requires building new interactive flow on finish step.
Adoption has high drop-off, but tutorial/prep screens consistently yield low or zero effect.
Reordering onboarding flows is a proven winner and strong support mail evidence (8 emails) backs fixing sign-in timing.
Major structural overhauls and path redesigns historically cause performance drops.
Account persistence hints are explicitly noted as harmful in earlier tests despite support emails.
Shortcut copy and desktop control flows delivered solid historical wins with low config-only cost.
Targeting the highest drop-off step (adoption at 64.2%) with improved select layouts has proven high historical success.
Wait/progress indicators show low-to-no effect in previous iterations, though cost is low.
